Run via tests/harness/gate.py <this file> (L0+L1; calls tests/harness/coverage_audit.py) and
tests/harness/mutation.py <this file> (L2).
MODULE: frontend/operation.py -- the PUBLIC named-operation construction vocabulary a CodeSpec
declares BEFORE a schedule compiles it. It is NOT a noise/mechanism model, NOT evaluator truth,
NOT a serialized channel payload: just OperationSpec (one named op + validated public metadata),
OperationSet (a validated non-empty duplicate-free collection), and the name-canonicalization +
default/coercion helpers. It imports NEITHER torch NOR quimb (dataclasses + a sibling
frontend.metadata_guard.validate_public_metadata), so EVERY public unit is CPU-PURE and IN-SCOPE
for full L0+L1+L2 -- out_of_scope is therefore {} (the AST reconcile refuses any gpu_bound claim
on a torch-less module -> expect ZERO out_of_scope).
NINE public units (AST reconcile _public_units_in_module: top-level public defs + every public
method of a top-level class INCLUDING the load-bearing __post_init__ dunder + the @property):
* OperationSpec.__post_init__   -- canonicalizes name (canonical_operation_name) + validates
public metadata (validate_public_metadata); rewrites both frozen fields in place.
* OperationSpec.to_manifest     -- {'name', 'metadata'(copy)} JSON-safe dict.
* OperationSet.__post_init__    -- coerces to a tuple; raises on empty; raises on duplicate
operation names (count>1); stores the coerced tuple.
* OperationSet.names            -- tuple of the member operation names.
* OperationSet.require          -- canonicalizes each required name; raises listing the sorted
missing set + the declared names when any is absent.
* OperationSet.to_manifest      -- list of each member's to_manifest().
* canonical_operation_name      -- strip/lower + alias map + ALLOWED membership guard (raise on
unsupported, message carries the ORIGINAL name repr + sorted ALLOWED set).
* default_memory_operations     -- the fixed (prep0, stabilizer_round, final_readout) tuple.
* as_operation_set              -- identity on an OperationSet else wrap each element (spec
kept, name coerced via OperationSpec).
The private module constants _ALIASES / ALLOWED_OPERATION_NAMES are NOT public units but ARE
mutated by mutmut (module-level literals): a wrapped alias key/value or ALLOWED member makes the
corresponding canonical/round-trip name fail its ALLOWED-membership guard -> raise -> the pin
test errors -> the mutant is killed. Every ALLOWED name is round-tripped and both aliases pinned
so every constant-literal mutant is covered.
L2 DISCIPLINE (100% coverage != discrimination).
* canonical_operation_name: all SIX ALLOWED names round-trip to themselves (kills each frozenset
member wrap); both aliases pin ('prepp'->'prep_plus', 'prepm'->'prep_minus'); case+whitespace
('  PREP_Plus ' -> 'prep_plus') make .strip()/.lower() load-bearing; the `not in` guard is
killed both ways (valid->no raise, unsupported->raise); the raise message is pinned EXACTLY via
assert_raises_exact (kills the f-string wrap/case/None mutants a substring match leaves
surviving) AND uses the ORIGINAL name repr (a mixed-case invalid pins name!r != out).
* OperationSpec.__post_init__: an UPPER/space name is coerced (.name pinned to the canonical
lower form -- kills the 'name' setattr-key wrap); the stored metadata is the validated COPY
(is-not the input dict -- kills the 'metadata' setattr-key wrap); a reserved metadata key is
rejected with the EXACT message carrying the OperationSpec(<name>).metadata label (kills the
label f-string wrap + proves validate_public_metadata is load-bearing).
* OperationSpec.to_manifest: the EXACT {'name','metadata'} dict is pinned vs an INDEPENDENT
literal + the metadata is a COPY (is-not the spec's) + assert_discriminates a field-drift.
* OperationSet.__post_init__: empty -> exact 'must contain at least one operation'; a UNIQUE
multi-op set constructs (kills count `>`->`>=` and `1`->`0`); a DUPLICATE raises the exact
'duplicate frontend operations [...]' (single + two-distinct sorted, reversed input still
sorted -> kills a dropped sorted / `1`->`2`); a LIST input is stored as a TUPLE (kills the
'operations' setattr-key wrap + proves tuple() coercion).
* OperationSet.names: the EXACT names tuple is pinned + assert_discriminates a wrong member.
* OperationSet.require: all-present returns None (no raise) through tuple/alias/upper routes;
the missing-required raise is tripped through EVERY input route (tuple, list, set, and an
alias whose CANONICAL form appears in the message) with the EXACT message via
assert_raises_exact (kills the set-difference `-`->`+`, the `if missing` negation, and the
f-string mutants).
* OperationSet.to_manifest: the EXACT list-of-dicts is pinned vs an INDEPENDENT literal +
assert_discriminates.
* default_memory_operations: the EXACT (prep0, stabilizer_round, final_readout) name tuple is
pinned (each literal's XX-wrap + None substitution -> construction raises -> killed) + each op
has empty metadata. CAVEAT: mutmut 3.6.0 ALSO emits an UPPERCASE case-swap per literal
('prep0'->'PREP0', ...); those THREE (mutmut_3/6/9) are byte-identical after
canonical_operation_name's .strip().lower() -> GENUINE EQUIVALENTS (proven vs the mutants/ tree),
NOT killable. See the harness.mutation_gate override below.
* as_operation_set: an OperationSet is returned by IDENTITY (is); a name-list is wrapped; a
mixed [spec, name] keeps the spec object by IDENTITY and wraps the name (kills the ternary
always-else, which would re-wrap the spec -> raise) + assert_discriminates.
REACHABILITY (the D13/D18/D19 default-arg / guard-route lesson -- PROBED through the PUBLIC entry
points, never asserted). Every raising guard (canonical unsupported-name, OperationSpec metadata
reserved-key via the label, OperationSet empty + duplicate, require missing) is tripped through a
real construction/call route with the EXACT message. CORRECTION (verified vs the mutants/ tree):
mutmut 3.6.0 emits BOTH an 'XX<s>XX' wrap AND an UPPERCASE case-swap per string literal. The XX-wraps
and None-substitutions all FAIL canonical_operation_name's ALLOWED-membership guard -> raise -> killed.
BUT the uppercase case-swaps of default_memory_operations' own already-canonical INPUT literals
('prep0'->'PREP0' etc.; mutmut_3/6/9) are byte-identical after .strip().lower() -> a MASKED fraction of
3/23 (measured ceiling 20/23=0.8696 = 20/20 KILLABLE killed). .strip().lower() is a legitimate public
canonicalization contract (case-insensitive names + _ALIASES + OperationSet.require canonicalizes its
args), documented via the harness.mutation_gate bar override below -- NOT a src-cleanup candidate
(unlike D19's incidental field .upper()). NO exemptions + NO out_of_scope: every unit is CPU-pure and
every branch is REACHABLE through a public entry point (checked, not assumed).

mutation_gate._note: D24 ceiling is 20/23=0.8696 = 20/20 KILLABLE mutants killed (100%). The 3 survivors (default_memory_operations x_..._mutmut_3/6/9) are mutmut 3.6.0 UPPERCASE case-swaps of the module's own canonical INPUT literals: 'prep0'->'PREP0', 'stabilizer_round'->'STABILIZER_ROUND', 'final_readout'->'FINAL_READOUT'. Each is BYTE-IDENTICAL to orig after OperationSpec.__post_init__ -> canonical_operation_name -> .strip().lower() (verified against mutants/src/error_coupling_simulator/frontend/operation.py), so no test input can distinguish them: GENUINE EQUIVALENTS. .strip().lower() is a LEGITIMATE public canonicalization contract (case-insensitive operation names + _ALIASES prepp/prepm + OperationSet.require canonicalizes its args), NOT D19-style incidental redundancy, so the honest fix is this documented bar override (cf. D14 accepted NoiseBuilder case equivalents), NOT dropping the normalization from src to game the metric. Standing criterion: incidental-redundant normalization -> de-dup (D19); legitimate canonicalization contract -> bar-override + document (D24).
